transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-11-05 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Rory (Redwood SE), Lena (VantageMed Procurement), Arjun (VantageMed Legal), Sophie (VantageMed Security), Tom (CTO)

Auto-summary: Quick alignment on MSA redline hotspots (egress, indemnity), confirm SLA phrasing (latency p95/p99, credits), ask for SOC2 iso docs + network diagram, agree to pilot pricing draft.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in, we'll go 45, 50 mins ish, and try to surface the legal/ procurement hotspots up front
00:18 Lena (Procurement): thanks Maya, yeah we have a pretty tight window — procurement committee meets 11/18 so want to understand gating points, pricing and any dpa/data residency notes
00:33 Rory (SE): quick intro from our side, i'll cover technical constraints for dedicated pools, kms and ingress/egress flow, and i'll call out where we can be flexible on SLAs
00:47 Arjun (Legal): great, main things are MSA indemnity language on egress, terms around sub processors in the DPA and auditability for data access logs
01:05 Sophie (Security): and KMS — we need to know if Redwood can support our key management (bring-your-own-key HSM via cloud KMS or customer HSM). also where kms lives for EU data
01:22 Tom (CTO): and from a product lens, latency targets and predictable costs are big. we may start hosted then move to dedicated within pilot if economics work
01:35 Maya: perfect, let's tee up the MSA first. there's a redline we circulated; main ask from you was to limit egress liability and specify that we only charge for egress where required by law/region, right?
01:54 Lena: Correct. Also we need clearer billing paths for egress for EU exports and any associated fees. procurement wants that line item in the rate sheet for approval
02:10 Rory: one clarifying point — when we say egress here, do you mean network egress or model output egress? we sometimes conflate token export vs data export to third parties
02:26 Arjun: network egress — transfer out of EU region. model outputs are fine as long as we have DPA assurances, but network fees are a procurement blocker
02:40 Maya: noted. we'll add a line in the term sheet for region-specific egress fees. i'll flag that in the next_steps.
02:55 Sophie: on KMS, is bring-your-own-key supported for Redwood Private? we saw mention of HSM integration in the docs but need the exact flow; also rotation, split keys, and audit logs
03:10 Rory: yes for Private we support customer-managed KMS, and we can integrate with common cloud KM S providers and some HSM flows. caveat: for hosted api there's a different surface — hosted supports envelope encryption but keys are in our managed KMS unless you opt for Private
03:30 Sophie: envelope encryption? can you spell that out — what data is encrypted at rest vs in transit vs in memory (kv cache)?
03:41 Rory: sure, at-rest encryption for model artifacts and user data on disk, in-transit TLS for all network traffic. KV cache is kept in memory on the serving nodes and is encrypted in mem when using Private with our KMS binding. i may have miss-said that earlier — mem encryption is an optional runtime flag for Private deployments
04:03 Tom: what's the operational burden to run Private? we have a small infra team and want low friction
04:12 Rory: Private has a control plane you can host in your VPC, or we can do a managed appliance. Dedicated is middle ground — dedicated GPU pool in redwood infra with tenancy isolation. Private on-prem needs more ops but gives the KMS and network control you want
04:36 Lena: procurement will require defined rollback and termination paths in the MSA. what happens to customer data at termination and how long do you retain backups?
04:48 Maya: good — our standard is 90 days data retention post-termination unless otherwise negotiated; snapshots can be purged on earlier schedule if requested. we'll put that in the redline notes
05:01 Arjun: 90 days seems long for us, for EU data we might need 30 days, can we make retention region-specific in the DPA?
05:12 Rory: technically yes, we can parameterize retention by region in Private or Dedicated; for hosted we'll need contractual language to limit backups in EU region and apply a 30-day retention
05:29 Sophie: and audit logs. we need access to immutable audit logs for model access and admin operations for a 12 month window, ideally exportable to our SIEM
05:42 Rory: we provide audit logs for admin ops and request traces; logs are available via syslog export or s3 delivery from the control plane for Private and Dedicated. hosted has an export endpoint but with retention tiers
06:00 Lena: can you point to the exact doc? we didn't find the export examples in the pkg
06:05 Maya: yes i'll put link in follow-up — https://redwood.ai/docs/sla-and-logs (note: placeholder)
06:12 Arjun: switching to SLA specifics — procurement wants p95 and p99 SLOs for the API, along with credit mechanisms. our ops lead wants to cap latency at 500ms p95 for embeddings and 1.5s p95 for small gen convo. is that feasible?
06:36 Rory: embeddings p95 500ms is aggressive depending on model and sequence length. for our curated smaller embedding models on Dedicated we can hit 300–400ms p95; for hosted it depends on tenant burst. For gen, 1.5s p95 for short context is plausible on dedicated but for long context it's longer
07:00 Tom: that suggests we should pilot embeddings on dedicated pool then route heavier gen to hosted. can we have routing policy in the agreement?
07:10 Maya: yes policy-based routing is a feature — we can commit to a traffic-split in the pilot SLA. we'll capture that in the pilot term sheet
07:20 Arjun: about credits — many vendors offer service credits as a percent of monthly invoice after 3 consecutive SLA misses. procurement wants a defined credit table and cap (we usually accept up to 25% cap).
07:36 Maya: standard redwood credit table tiers will be provided; we can discuss cap in negotiation, but our default cap is 30% for mission critical SLA tiers; we can look to reduce to 25% for enterprise commitments
07:50 Sophie: any security exception process? if there is an incident we need incident response timing, RU time to acknowledge, and post-mortem delivery timeline
08:02 Rory: incident response: we ack within 30 minutes for Sev1, initial triage within 4 hours, and a post-mortem within 5 business days. that'll be included in the incident response appendix.
08:17 Lena: procurement will want to know for the pilot what commit and what discount is available — is there a self-serve estimator?
08:27 Maya: we have a pricing worksheet; for pilots we typically do a 3-month commit with a pilot discount and capacity reservations. i'll share a draft term sheet with numbers; we need to know expected QPS and average seq length to produce accurate pricing
08:45 Tom: we'll run an internal perf test simulating 100 QPS of small embedding requests and 10 concurrent gen sessions, average seq ~256 tokens.
08:58 Rory: good, that helps. for those numbers, Dedicated pool of X cards would give predictable lat and cost, i'll estimate in the sheet
09:12 Arjun: back to DPA and sub processors — we need a list of third-party subprocessors (e.g., cloud infra partners) and a standard flow for notifications if a new subprocessor is added
09:28 Maya: we'll add a subprocessor list; our major partners are public cloud providers and a managed infra partner. notifications follow our DPA clause with 30 day notice for new subprocessors unless required by law
09:42 Sophie: data residency: if we route EU traffic to EU region, can you ensure no log replication to US?
09:50 Rory: yes, for Private and Dedicated we can ensure control plane and logs stay in-region. for hosted we'll need to default to region isolation but some monitoring telemetry may be ingested centrally — we'll flag that as an item in the redline
10:10 Lena: ok good. procurement asks for a one-page risktable summarizing residual risk and mitigations for governance review
10:18 Maya: we'll produce a risktable and RAG status for each item — MSA, DPA, KMS, SLA, pricing.
10:25 Arjun: small legal nuance — indemnity for data breaches. we typically accept indemnity limited to direct damages and not punitive. what's Redwood's stance?
10:38 Maya: we limit indemnity to direct damages and have caps tied to annual fees; we can discuss exceptions but that's the starting point. we'll put in the redline
10:50 Sophie: controls around admin creds — RBAC and SSO. Can we enforce SSO + SCIM provisioning and role-based admin separation?
11:02 Rory: yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning supported; RBAC roles available via console and can be synced to your IdP. privileged access is auditable via our admin logs.
11:18 Tom: timeline question — if we sign pilot by 11/18, how quickly can we be in pilot?
11:25 Maya: for dedicated we need 4–6 weeks to provision GPUs and config routing; Private/VPC options add lead time. If we agree to a small dedicated pool for pilot we can aim for 3 weeks with accelerated provisioning and a provisioning fee
11:42 Lena: procurement will run approvals if the MSA redline is small. looking at the list so far, it seems feasible to route to committee 11/18 if we get the redline and pricing sheet by 11/10
11:55 Maya: good — action items captured. any other blockers?
12:02 Arjun: one more — escrow and source access. procurement may want limited escrow terms for critical components, what is Redwood's position?
12:14 Maya: we offer an escrow path for enterprise customers; details depend on commitment level. we'll put a note and propose escrow terms in the commercial appendix
12:26 Sophie: ok thanks, that's helpful.
12:30 Maya: quick recap — Maya to send MSA redline and pilot term sheet by 11/10; Rory to share network/VPC diagram + SLA examples by 11/08; Sophie to send KMS/key rotation questions by 11/07; Arjun to flag DPA exceptions by 11/09. Redwood will also attach SOC2/ISO docs.
12:54 Tom: sounds good, i'll loop in ops for the perf sim and get data over to you
13:02 Lena: procurement will expect the risktable and one-pager. thanks everyone
13:10 Maya: thanks all will follow up via email and share links: MSA redline (drive), pricing worksheet (sheet), networking diagram (pdf), compliance pack (s3 link)
13:28 End of meeting

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-recognition of product names (Redwood Dedicated sometimes transcribed as Red wood Dedicated), some timestamps approximate. Links referenced will be sent in follow-up email.
